objects.description: Enumeration of file/resource kinds handled by the system, primarily shader and texture assets. Values indicate fragment/vertex shaders, images (including cubemaps and bump maps), geometry data, and GLSL include/dependency files.
Record describing a single watched file. Holds the file path, its FileType, a last-change marker (likely a timestamp or revision counter), and a vertical-flip flag for texture assets.
Alias for a dynamic array (std::vector) of WatchFile entries. Used to manage collections of watched files.

Concrete command type holding a trigger string, a formula string, a human-readable description, a callable to execute the command (takes the input string and returns success as bool), and a mutex flag indicating whether execution should be mutually exclusive. Provides a default and a convenience initializing constructor. No destructor or copy/move customization is defined; it uses the defaults.

Alias for a vector of Command objects. Behaves like std::vector<Command> with contiguous storage and value semantics. Construction is via standard std::vector constructors; no special constructors are provided in this header.
Alias for a high_resolution_clock time_point. Used as a timestamp for when a statistic/track started. Underlying type is implementation-defined by std::chrono for high_resolution_clock.
A single timing sample expressed in milliseconds, holding start, end, and computed duration for one measured interval.

Aggregates timing data for a named track: the current call stack/name, a start timestamp, collected timing samples, and the running average duration in milliseconds. Lifetimes of contained fields are owned by the struct instance.

A profiling/measurement utility that manages timing tracks and samples. It can start/stop a session, begin/end named tracks, compute framerate, and generate log strings for samples and averages. Ownership: holds a map of track name to StatTrack and a list of active track names. Construction/destruction specifics are not provided in this header; behavior is inferred from member names.

functions.name: Tracker::Tracker
functions.description: Default constructor for Tracker. Initializes a new tracking instance for timing/metrics collection. Use it to create an object before invoking start/stop and logging methods.
requirements: Object must be constructed before any member function is called.
No arguments required; uses default initialization.

functions.name: Tracker::~Tracker
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Tracker. Cleans up resources associated with the tracking instance. Enables safe deletion via base-class pointers.
requirements: Do not call the destructor directly; it is invoked automatically when the object goes out of scope or via delete.
If subclassing, ensure derived destructors are virtual or rely on this base virtual destructor.

functions.name: Tracker::start
functions.description: Begins tracking. Typically sets the tracker into a running state and captures a baseline time reference to compute durations and framerate.
requirements: Should be called before collecting timing data or calling stop().
Calling start() on an already running tracker may be a no-op or reset state; exact behavior is unknown from this header.

functions.name: Tracker::stop
functions.description: Stops tracking. Typically marks the tracker as not running and finalizes timing accumulation used by logging and framerate reporting.
requirements: Should be called after a preceding start() to end a tracking session.
Calling stop() when not running may be a no-op; exact behavior is unknown from this header.

functions.name: Tracker::begin
functions.description: Marks the start of a named timing section (track). Use this to begin measuring a specific code region identified by _track.
requirements: _track identifies the section to be measured and should be paired with a subsequent end(_track) call.
begin/end calls for the same _track should be properly nested and paired; behavior for overlapping or mismatched pairs is unspecified.
The tracker should be in an appropriate state to record timing (typically after start()); exact enforcement is unknown from this header.

functions.name: Tracker::end
functions.description: Marks the end of a named timing section (track) previously started with begin(_track). Completes a sample for the specified track.
requirements: Must correspond to a preceding begin(_track) for the same _track value.
begin/end calls for a given _track should be balanced; behavior on missing or extra end() calls is unspecified.
The tracker should be in an appropriate state to record timing (typically after start()); exact enforcement is unknown from this header.

functions.name: Tracker::getFramerate
functions.description: Returns the current or recent framerate estimate as a double (frames per second). Computation details are not specified in the header.
requirements: Callable at any time; returned value may depend on whether tracking has been started and recent samples exist (unspecified).
No arguments; return value semantics (e.g., range, NaN on error) are unknown.

functions.name: Tracker::logSamples
functions.description: Generates a textual report of recorded samples for all tracks. The returned string is suitable for logging or console output.
requirements: Callable after samples have potentially been recorded via begin/end; behavior with no samples is unspecified.
No arguments; returns a std::string containing the report.

functions.name: Tracker::logAverage
functions.description: Generates a textual report summarizing average durations for all tracks. The exact format and averaging window are not specified.
requirements: Callable after samples have potentially been recorded via begin/end; behavior with no samples is unspecified.
Returns a std::string containing the report.

functions.name: Tracker::logFramerate
functions.description: Generates a textual report of the current or recent framerate. The exact computation and format are not specified.
requirements: Callable at any time; output may depend on whether start/stop have been used and whether samples exist (unspecified).
Returns a std::string containing the report.

functions.name: Tracker::isRunning
functions.description: Returns true if the tracker is currently running (i.e., between start() and stop()); false otherwise.
requirements: Const method; does not modify object state.
Callable at any time.

functions.name: findId
functions.signature: bool findId(const std::string& program, const char* id);
functions.description: Searches the given program text for an identifier. The header comment says "Search for one apearance" (sic), implying the function checks for a single occurrence of id in program. The exact success criterion (at least one vs. exactly one occurrence; case sensitivity; token vs. substring match) is not documented and remains unknown. Typical usage would pass shader/source text in program and an identifier name in id to detect its presence.
requirements: program must be a valid, initialized std::string reference containing the text to be scanned.
id must be a non-null, null-terminated C string pointing to the identifier to search for.

The matching rules (substring vs. tokenized, case sensitivity, and whether the function expects exactly one occurrence) are unknown from the header and should be confirmed from implementation or docs.
Return value semantics beyond boolean success/failure are not documented; callers should be prepared for either interpretation (found at least once or found exactly once).

functions.name: getBufferSize
functions.description: Parses _source to obtain the size of a buffer named _name and returns it as a 3D vector. The comment indicates that a component value of -1.0 means the buffer has a fixed size (semantics ambiguous: whether -1.0 appears in all components or signals a non-dynamic, compile-time size). Intended usage is to analyze shader/source code and extract declared buffer dimensions for the named buffer.
requirements: _source must be a valid, initialized std::string reference containing the code/text to be parsed.
_name must be a valid, initialized std::string reference naming the buffer to query.
The coordinate system and units of the returned glm::vec3 are not documented; interpretation of -1.0 markers is only partially described and should be validated against implementation.
Behavior when _name is not found in _source is not documented (e.g., return value defaults, error signaling); callers should handle unexpected return values.

functions.name: countBuffers

requirements: _source must be a valid, initialized std::string reference.

Return value is an integer count; negative values are not indicated by the signature, but error signaling behavior is otherwise unknown.
